Subject: Quick follow-up + next step: Dedicated capacity sizing call

Hi Tara —

Thanks again for taking the time earlier today. Quick recap from our discovery:
- Primary use case: document ingestion + extraction and a chat assistant for clinical ops.
- Expected steady-state traffic: ~120 QPS of short prompts (avg 150 tokens) during business hours with spikes up to ~550 QPS for batch runs.
- Latency goal: p90 < 350ms for chat queries; acceptable degradation to 600ms during large batch windows.
- Data controls: VPC + KMS required, SOC2 evidence needed.

Next step: schedule a dedicated capacity sizing session with our solutions engineering team to map throughput/latency to GPU footprint and recommended batching/kv-cache settings. Vivek is our SE who runs these. Suggested agenda (30–45m):
1) Confirm traffic profile and SLOs
2) Review model choices + quantization trade-offs
3) Sizing recommendation and cost estimate
4) Action items and timeline for Dedicated trial

Are you available for a 45-minute slot next week? I can propose Thu 4/15 10am PT or Fri 4/16 9am PT — happy to work around your calendar.

Attaching the short traffic snapshot you shared and a Redwood Dedicated overview to help prep.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0123

Hi Tara / team —

Thanks for scheduling — looking forward to the call on Fri 4/16 09:00am PT. To make the session as useful as possible, here's a proposed agenda and the minimal data we need up front:

Proposed agenda (45m):
- 5m intro + success criteria
- 10m traffic profile deep-dive (QPS distribution, burst characteristics, sequence lengths)
- 15m model recommendation + quantization/latency tradeoffs
- 10m sizing: GPU count & estimated throughput, KV cache strategy, batching settings
- 5m next steps and pilot timeline

Data request (small):
- Steady-state QPS and 95/99th percentile burst QPS (per minute if possible)
- Percentiles of sequence length (p50/p90/p99) or distribution sample
- Desired p90 latency SLO for interactive queries
- Typical concurrency per user session (if applicable)
- Any retention/kv-cache window (how long you want to reuse past tokens)

If you can paste the values into the doc or reply to this thread, I’ll model two sizing options: "conservative" (guaranteed p90 SLO) and "cost-optimized" (occasional p95 degradation). I’ll also include a ballpark monthly cost for Redwood Dedicated and assumptions.

Thanks — Vivek

Thanks Vivek — adding the numbers here so you have them before Friday:
- Steady-state: 120 QPS (8am–6pm ET)
- Burst (p95): 420 QPS (sustained for ~10–15 minutes during morning ramp)
- Overnight batch: up to 550 QPS for bulk jobs (can be scheduled off-peak)
- Sequence lengths: p50=140 tokens, p90=480 tokens, p99=1,900 tokens (~4% long-tail)
- Desired p90 latency SLO: 350ms for interactive queries
- Concurrency per session: typically 1–3 concurrent requests per user
- KV-cache window: 10 minutes for session context reuse

Also attaching a sanitized sample traffic CSV. Looking forward to the call.

Best,
Tara
